title: SKU Flexband & SLA Matrix for Dedicated GPU Packages
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Define a compact, enterprise-friendly SKU matrix for Redwood Dedicated that unifies reserved GPU commitments, burst credits, and autoscale bands with clear SLA tiers and contract language suitable for security questionnaire review.

Background: Customers ask for predictable throughput for production LLM endpoints while retaining the ability to absorb short spikes. Current offers are fragmented across legacy reserved SKUs and ad-hoc burst add-ons. Legal and Sales also need contract language and pre-filled answers for common security questionnaire items tied to Dedicated (VPC + on-prem variants).

Scope:
- Propose 3 core commitment bands (Committed, Flex, Enterprise) across GPU count and baseline throughput.
- Define burst credit model (minutes of burst per month, pro-rated credit top-ups) and clear throttling/overflow policies.
- Specify autoscale policy tiers (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) with documented expected latency/throughput deltas and cost multipliers.
- Map SLA tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold) to uptime % and latency p90 targets, plus remediation credits.
- Create contract language templates and pre-populated SQ responses for common auditor questions (data residency, encryption, incident response, RBAC, KMS).

Acceptance criteria:
- A pricing table with list prices and discounted committed rates for each band for 3 common footprint profiles (small: 4–8 GPUs, medium: 16–32 GPUs, large: 64+ GPUs).
- A burst credit calculator with examples (5% baseline, 20% burst for 30 minutes, sample invoices).
- Autoscale policy definitions with expected steady-state cost multipliers (e.g., 1.0x baseline, 1.4x balanced, 1.9x aggressive).
- SLA language that legal signs off on and that feeds into playbook answers for at least 10 common SQ items.
- A short sales one-pager and an enablement checklist for AMs.

Deliverables:
- SKU matrix CSV (attached) and canonical markdown for pricing page copy.
- Contract clause snippets (SLA, termination, overage billing, audit rights).
- Security questionnaire canonical answers and pointer doc to config options (VPC, KMS, audit logs).

Risks and trade-offs:
- Simplicity vs granularity: fewer SKUs mean faster quoting but less tailored economics for very large customers.
- Burst economics: setting burst too generous may cannibalize committed revenue; too restrictive harms adoption.
- Legal/Compliance alignment may require additional scoping for on-prem variants (air-gapped installs).
